content:
Apple has released the first developer beta of iOS 27.2 for iPhone. This update comes shortly after iOS 27 was officially rolled out to all users on Monday, and it also skips iOS 27.1, which Apple has positioned as an update tailored for the iPhone Duo.

iOS 27.2 beta 1 arrives before iOS 27.1 beta

Today's beta release follows the official launch of iOS 27 on September 14. The new version is a fairly substantial update, weighing in at 22GB.

Apple has previously detailed how the iOS 27.1 SDK lets developers take full advantage of the iPhone Duo's display. You can learn more here about how apps will appear on the iPhone Duo depending on which iOS version they target.

However, today's release of iOS 27.2 developer beta 1 currently skips over iOS 27.1.

Apple appears to want to hold back the iPhone Duo-specific code for closer to the new hardware's launch in October. Developers still need to prepare for the new device, though. Apple has said the relevant tools are expected to be ready by the end of September.

Apple has also previewed other changes coming to all iPhones next month, including a redesigned Apple Health app and expanded Siri AI capabilities.

Apple confirmed this week: 'Siri AI will debut as a more capable, more human-like conversational assistant, with personalised contextual understanding, rich common-sense knowledge, on-screen content awareness, and more cross-system app actions. Siri AI is currently available in English as a beta, with French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish support rolling out starting in October.'

This may give us a rough sense of when the final version will arrive.

Once we actually install and try out the first build, we'll be able to learn more about what Apple has included this time.

We'll cover what's new and everything else in today's new beta in a separate roundup. Stay tuned for our ongoing iOS 27.2 beta coverage.
